body.answer:
Nursing Programs Office: Its published phone is (201) 684-7749, Fax: (201) 684-7954, and it is in Adler Center for Nursing Excellence 215. It does not publish a general email; its pages were checked October 21, 2026. [1]
Registrar: Email: reg@ramapo.edu; phone: (201) 684-7695; Fax: (201) 684-7956; Beth Foster Associate Registrar: (201) 684-7324; Jill Pierson Assistant Registrar: (201) 684-7288; Kathy Larsen Graduation Coordinator & Transfer Evaluator: (201) 684-7296; Reilly Cox System / Curriculum Analyst: (201) 684-7323; Lillian R. Martinez Office Coordinator: (201) 684-7781; Vanessa Ramos Support Representative: (201) 684-7320. The Registrar is in D-224. [2]
Office of the Provost: The undergraduate grade appeal procedure is here: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature. [3]
1. A grade appeal requires supporting documentation. Possible grounds include computational error, factual information not considered, or an alleged College Policy violation.
2. Within twenty calendar days after grades are posted, send the course instructor a written appeal by email or certified letter and provide supporting documentation.
3. You and the instructor should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences; you have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination.
4. If you and the instructor agree an adjustment is warranted, the instructor sends an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request, explanatory reasons, and supporting documentation to the Dean of the academic unit sponsoring the course. After the Dean approves, the request goes to the Registrar.
5. If you cannot agree and want to continue, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean may confer with you and the instructor jointly or independently, review documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff as appropriate. The Deans have 15 calendar days to decide. If a change is warranted, the Dean sends an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advises you and the instructor in writing. If not warranted, you and the instructor are informed in writing by email.
6. If the Dean’s opinion does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. Send a written statement by email or certified letter explaining your position and including evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost may reject a request without clear evidence of factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. Only appeals fully discussed at instructor and Dean level are considered. After conferring with you, the Dean, and instructor and reviewing documentation, the Provost or designee may approve or decline the appeal and advise you, the instructor, and Dean of the final recommendation. The decision is rendered within 15 calendar days and is final. [3]

value.section_words: the course instructor forwards an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request, including explanatory reasons and all supporting documentation, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course. Upon the Dean’s approval, the Instructor Grade Adjustment Request is forwarded to the Registrar. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination. If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost. The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable. Such a petition must be made within twenty calendar days of the final, written determination by the Dean. The Office of the Provost reserves the right to hear the petition and will reject any request that does not offer clear evidence that the Dean made a factual mistake, violated school policy, or otherwise acted outside the purview of the Dean. The Provost or their designee will consider only those grade appeals that have previously received full deliberative discussion at both the instructor and Dean level. After conferring with the student, Dean, and course instructor and reviewing the pertinent documentation, the Provost or their designee may approve or decline the student’s grade appeal. The Provost or their designee will advise the student, the course instructor, and the Dean of their final recommendation. The decision will be rendered within 15 calendar days. The decision of the Provost or their designee is final.

Upon the Dean’s approval, the Instructor Grade Adjustment Request is forwarded to the Registrar. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination. If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost. The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable. Such a petition must be made within twenty calendar days of the final, written determination by the Dean. The Office of the Provost reserves the right to hear the petition and will reject any request that does not offer clear evidence that the Dean made a factual mistake, violated school policy, or otherwise acted outside the purview of the Dean. The Provost or their designee will consider only those grade appeals that have previously received full deliberative discussion at both the instructor and Dean level. After conferring with the student, Dean, and course instructor and reviewing the pertinent documentation, the Provost or their designee may approve or decline the student’s grade appeal. The Provost or their designee will advise the student, the course instructor, and the Dean of their final recommendation. The decision will be rendered within 15 calendar days. The decision of the Provost or their designee is final.
